blind.why: Teammates running away from the camera (p_runners_behind.png vs t1_010). CS2 runners carry their weapon low with a natural arm swing and lean, and each has a varied silhouette. Ours run with both forearms raised vertically and elbows flared out (pistol run), under horizontal cream pauldrons, so the upper body reads as a T-shape and they look like they are surrendering.

A single enemy in a sunlit open area at 5-10 m (read_s7_tide_5m vs t4_005). Ours reads instantly because Tide cyan against sandstone is excellent, but the pose is stiff, with both hands held up at the visor, and the body is a stack of boxes. The CS2 model is posed naturally and is just as legible from its value contrast. Close call: ours wins on colour and loses on posture.

An enemy at about 15 m (far_s5_ember_15m_1 vs t2_028). The CS2 CT is a crisp dark silhouette against a bright wall. Our Ember stands in the shade under the B-site pergola, and its near-black umber suit merges with the dark wood posts. Only the cream helmet and a few muted orange stripes show, so he is easy to miss.

Model and lineup quality (gal_lineup2 vs ss_0). In CS2 each character has its own silhouette, and the weapons sit at the shoulder with the support hand on the handguard. Ours are ten identical box robots with oversized shoulder pads. The rifle, sniper and shotgun are all held vertically at the sternum, so from the front the weapon class cannot be read.

biggest_gap: Hands are not attached to the weapon, and the hold poses are unconvincing. (1) Reload bug: from about 0.6 s to 2.0 s into the 2.4 s reload, the rifle floats on its own in front of the visor, tilted 45 degrees up, while both hands sit at belly height (one at the pouch, one empty). Repro: ?test=1&seed=1&scene=character-gallery&ui=0&layout=pair, debug.pose('reload'), advance(1.1), cam(90,5,4.4) -> shots/critic-avatars-r4/gal2_reload_side.png and z_reload_f3.png. (2) Pistol run raises both forearms vertically with the elbows flared sideways (p_runners_behind.png, seed 3 live +2.2 s). (3) Rifle, sniper and shotgun holds put the gun vertically at the sternum, so from the front the weapon is a dot and the class cannot be read (gal_lineup2.png). (4) Throw: across 1.1 s there is no visible wind-up arc. The canister just hangs at shoulder height and the free arm hangs limp (gal2_throw_anim.png). CS2 keeps the support hand on the handguard through locomotion. Its reload swaps the magazine with the support hand while the firing hand stays on the grip, and its weapons sit shouldered, so the gun class shows in the silhouette. Fix: pin the weapon to handR at all times with two-bone IK and drive handL to waypoints on the gun (mag well, then pouch, then mag well). Lower the pistol-run forearms. Rotate long guns so they project forward from the shoulder.
other_gaps: Ember in shade still camouflages. The near-black umber suit with cream helmet and pads disappears against dark wood and shadowed sandstone at 15 m or more (far_s5_ember_15m_1, read_s2_ember_15m). The orange bands are too thin and too dim to carry team identity. Tide reads instantly everywhere, so the two teams are not equally readable. Widen or brighten the Ember emissive bands, or give the Ember silhouette a lighter rim.

Both teams share cream/white helmets and horizontal shoulder pads. When only a head and shoulders peek over cover, Ember and Tide look the same, which is the most common engagement view. Tint the helmet and pads by team.

Silhouette and proportions: in side view the head sits in front of the chest line (hunched), the pads stick straight out to the sides, and the boxy limbs have no hands or fingers. Every bot is the same model, with no per-player silhouette variety (gal_run_side, gal_lineup0).

The backpack and helmet crest are drawn but cannot be hit. A ray grid on runners at about 7 m/s from 7 m found 10-13% of drawn body pixels miss every capsule, mostly a 15 cm block on the back. Capsules also overhang the drawn legs, giving phantom hits on 12-17% of the drawn area (hitsyncB_s9_*.txt, hitsync_s6_*.txt). Render and hitbox lag is now 0, which is good.
Crouch-walk shows almost no visible leg motion over 0.35 s (gal_crouchWalk_anim). Strafe is a scissor-step with little weight shift.
Pink and white cosmetic trail sparkles on bots partly obscure the torso at mid range (p_runners_behind_2, read_s11_ember_5m).
bugs: Rifle floats with no hand on it during the middle of the reload (gal2_reload_side.png, z_reload_f3.png).

Spawn materialise does not include the held weapon or charm. At round start in the normal match flow (?test=1&seed=7&match=1, buy phase, about 0.3 s), teammates appear as a pair of feet plus a fully formed pistol floating at chest height, rotated vertically (rs_spawn_0.3.png, z_lineup.png). It repeats every round:start.
strengths: Hitboxes follow the animated bones, and render and hitbox root lag is now 0 at about 7 m/s.
Tide cyan is very readable at 5-50 m on this warm map, and Ember orange bands still show as a figure at 50 m in sunlight.
Cheap to render: about 4.3 draw calls and 4.7k triangles per visible actor including shadows (scene 118 calls vs 79 with characters hidden).
Plant kneel and press reads well. Run gait has decent lean and stride. No console errors during runs.
